scope: Second intensive review of three public-registry-labelled artifacts; no feed verdict used as behavioral evidence.

samples.identification: Firefox source-view capture of a DarkSword-labelled iOS exploitation/credential-export loader
analysis: Outer body id=viewsource contains escaped source markup and zero live script elements: opening the saved wrapper alone does not execute the represented script. The represented code is malicious; neither an infection nor successful exploitation is inferred.

Reconstructed the represented 13,187-byte script through HTML parsing, not regex removal of code. Traced main(): mobile UA parsing, Facebook/Instagram/Line exclusion, iOS 18.5/18.6 through 18.6.2 gate, six external module fetches, window.modules population and eval of the fetched loader. iOS >=26 appends a different remote script; iOS <18 appends an offscreen iframe.

After loader evaluation it appends pe_main.js, then native_bridge.js; its onload callback assigns readKeychain() to kc and sends that value in JSON data to an external POST with cmd=keychain_dump. A separate branch assigns getCryptoWalletFiles() to w and exports w with cmd=wallet_dump. Error and status reports are separate branches, not evidence that secrets were recovered.

Five QuickJS model runs with no host I/O, mocked fetch/native helpers and bounded runtime confirmed the gated loader/export path and excluded/alternative versions. Six mocked script fetches and two sentinel-bearing exports occurred for iOS 18.6.2; none of the remote code or endpoints was fetched.

samples.classifier: Atomscan says benign (level -1, confidence 0.991); retained as malicious represented content, with explicit inert-wrapper qualification.

analysis: Enumerated every tar member and inspected setup.py, PKG-INFO and the empty initializer. No other file payload or tar link is present.

setup() registers _I for install. _I.run delegates to install.run(self), then executes base64.b64decode of one literal. Independently decoded the entire literal to exactly print("quillmark installed") followed by newline and parsed the Python body. No network, secret access, command launch or persistence is in that body.

The encoded exec is an accurate dynamic-evaluation and concealment signal; retained all decoder/evaluator facts and suspicious b64decode-exec. Placeholder metadata and a custom hook establish neither impersonation nor a backdoor. Lack of useful functionality is not itself malicious.

The hostile corpus fixture has exactly the target SHA-256; moved it to this explicitly BENIGN focused-control directory and removed its wrong hostile expectation. The ordinary benign/ corpus unconditionally rejects suspicious objective traits, so putting it there would require erasing accurate concealment. The dedicated check instead asserts BENIGN with exactly the retained suspicious concealment finding.
missing_context: Publisher intent and real deployment context are unknown; those gaps do not turn a fully recovered status print into an attack.
samples.classifier: Archive remains hostile at level 1, confidence 99, probability field 0.9942017. Member setup.py remains benign by its model. This is a remaining archive-classifier false positive.

samples.identification: TikTok LIVE TypeScript project repackaged with an unrelated obfuscated Windows LuaJIT loader
analysis: The TypeScript source implements a plausible TikTool WebSocket client. package.json declares tiktool/tiktok-live-api as upstream, whereas the README promotes this repackager's nested Windows ZIP and instructs users to launch it and approve prompts. A library dependency name is not the basis for conviction.

Nested ZIP has exactly Application.cmd, loader.exe, lua51.dll and module.cso. Application.cmd runs start loader.exe module.cso. Rizin xrefs and disassembly traced luaL_loadfile and protected invocation in the LuaJIT CLI carrier. Runtime imports/exports and facts corroborate the interpreter role, without labelling the standard Lua DLL malicious on its own.

module.cso is text Lua, using numeric state flattening, decimal escapes, fragment-index reassembly, encrypted strings and environment indirection. A restricted Lua 5.1 runtime denied require ffi before any native interface could load, exposed the pure decryption closure, and combined it with block-local AST folding to recover 995 distinct ciphertext/seed constants (1990 evaluations including revisits). All OS, shell, network and native FFI access was absent.

Traced loader.bypass_defender == 1 to state 11457996. That block assembles comment-split powershell Start-Process, -Verb runAs, hidden-window options and Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $env:SystemDrive -ExclusionExtension .exe, .dll -Force, then invokes the command wrapper with show flag 0. This requests elevation; it proves neither a UAC bypass nor successful elevation.

Configuration-dependent autorun paths build schtasks /create /sc daily /st %02d:%02d /f, choose hour 10..14 and minute 0..59, add /tn and /tr action operands and pass the resulting command to execution. The source also has task dispatch, WinInet HTTP helpers, an external default endpoint and registry/graphics/native support. These latter neutral observations are retained without inventing a proved secret source-to-send chain or next-stage success.
samples.coverage: Existing two hostile behaviors in distinct evasion and persistence subdirectories plus all six suspicious findings are retained, including in the nested archive and decoded Lua member.

changes.reason: Unsupported backdoor/hostile inference from hook+Base64+exec. Quillmark is a concrete benign full-body match. Existing setup-hook metadata, Base64 decode, exec, direct decoder-to-exec flow, run-method-exec and suspicious concealment observations preserve all supported behavior; no duplicate contextual API rule added.

Same manifest/hook matchers, file types, archive scope and confidence. Name/description now include packaging hooks (PEP 517 backend alternatives included). Notable structural fact; removed unsupported impersonation ATT&CK and single-instance MBC B0024 mappings. Removed downgrades that would falsely turn this meaningful structure into baseline.

A run override near generic exec/eval/compile/process APIs is a neutral capability co-occurrence, not a suspicious installation attack; compile alone does not establish execution. All canonical API atoms and hook metadata remain. Four explicit attack consumers now inline the original alternatives and require their additional attack evidence in the local 10-line span. This is intentionally stricter than treating a nearby generic code operation as reusable attack evidence.

reference_audit.disposition: No directory selector was expanded to treat neutral packaging or execution as attack evidence. Retired standalone aliases are absent. The old Vitest suppression was incompatible with the Python-only generic observation; no new incompatible suppressor was propagated. All new rule placement uses an existing admitted leaf with 53 rules.

validation_performance_fixes.change: Removed 36 redundant (_)* sibling wildcards. Tree-sitter sibling patterns are already nonadjacent without dot anchors, so the same object fields, order alternatives, string limits and selector exclusions remain. All 20 existing boundary cases pass, including six field-order permutations and benign selector near misses. Added a wide-object performance probe with distant required fields.

Moved its unchanged impure-call query into metadata/lang/source/syntax/call::javascript-call-outside-table-helper-vocabulary and referenced it from unless. This incomplete context predicate is component severity; it asserts no execution or harmfulness. It has no count requirement, so finding one impure call proves the existing guard without enumerating every call under the parent profile's count requirement. The existing table matcher, count=3, import/constructor/error guards, platforms and scope remain unchanged. Added a performance probe exceeding 100,000 raw call captures.
